prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A breech catch mechanism for automatic and semi-automatic pistols includes a catch (502) of a breech comprising two longitudinal rails (400, 401) that are attached to pistol body or to an inserted container at one end in a rotary way and at the other end they are connected with a bridge (402). One of the rails (400, 401) is provided with an internal projection (405) protruding into a space between the rails (400, 401). The mechanism further includes the breech provided with a feeding bridge (250) and a cartridge feeder (500) positioned under the internal projection (405) and configured to push, after feeding of the last cartridge, from below against the internal projection (405), thus tilting the breech catch (502) from its basic position upward to an upper position in which the breech leans with its feeding bridge (250) against an outer surface (408) of the bridge (402) of the catch (502) of the breech to lock the breech in the rear position.

A breech catch mechanism for automatic and semi-automatic pistols includes a breech catch (502) comprising two longitudinal rails (400, 401), which are rotatably attached at one end to a pistol body or to an inserted container and connected at the other end by a bridge (402). One of the rails (400, 401) is provided with an internal projection (405) protruding into the space between the rails (400, 401).

The mechanism further includes a breech provided with a feeding bridge (250), and a cartridge feeder (500) positioned beneath the internal projection (405). One of the rails (400, 401) has an inward-facing projection (405) that extends into the gap between the rails. The arrangement also includes a breech equipped with a feeding bridge (250), as well as a cartridge feeder (500) located beneath the inward projection (405). The breech catch mechanism is intended for use in automatic and semi-automatic pistols, where it serves to hold the breech in its rearward position after the final cartridge has been fired or fed. The mechanism is constructed with two longitudinal rails arranged alongside one another. These rails are rotatably attached at one end, allowing the catch to tilt or pivot during operation, and they are joined together at the opposite end by a transverse bridge.

One of the rails is provided with an inwardly directed projection that extends into the space between the two rails. Beneath this projection is a cartridge feeder, which rises as cartridges are supplied. After the last cartridge has been fed, the feeder moves upward far enough to press against the internal projection on the rail.

This upward pressure causes the breech catch to tilt about its rotatable attachment point. As a result, the bridge connecting the two rails is raised into a position where it engages the breech. The breech is then prevented from moving forward and remains locked in its rear position against the catch bridge, indicating that the magazine or feeding mechanism is empty.

A breech catch mechanism for automatic and semi-automatic pistols is designed to hold the breech or slide in its rearward, open position after the last cartridge has been fired and fed from the magazine. The mechanism includes two longitudinal catch rails arranged on opposite sides of the firearm and mounted so that they can pivot relative to the pistol frame. These rails are connected to one another by a transverse catch bridge, forming a rigid catch element that can move upward and downward as a unit.

Within the mechanism, an inwardly directed projection is positioned so that it can be engaged by the cartridge feeder or magazine follower. While cartridges remain in the magazine, the follower is held below this projection by the ammunition stack, and the breech catch remains in its lowered, inactive position. In this condition, the breech or slide is free to move forward and rearward during normal cycling of the pistol.

After the last round has been fed into the chamber, the magazine follower rises to its uppermost position under the force of the magazine spring. As it rises, the follower engages the internal projection of the breech catch mechanism. This engagement causes the two longitudinal rails and their connecting bridge to pivot upward. The upward tilting movement places the catch bridge in the path of a corresponding feeding bridge or contact surface on the breech.

When the breech moves rearward after the final shot, the feeding bridge of the breech comes into contact with the raised catch bridge. This contact prevents the breech from returning forward, thereby locking it in the rear position. The open position of the breech clearly indicates that the pistol is empty and also facilitates rapid reloading, since the shooter can insert a loaded magazine and then release the breech to chamber the next round.

Because the catch mechanism is actuated directly by the magazine follower after the last cartridge has been fed, it provides dependable last-round hold-open operation without requiring complex additional components. The use of two pivoting longitudinal rails connected by a bridge ensures stable movement and even load distribution when the breech is arrested. This construction improves reliability, reduces the likelihood of misalignment or incomplete engagement, and provides a simple, durable breech catch arrangement suitable for both automatic and semi-automatic pistols.

**Abstract**

A breech catch mechanism for automatic and semi-automatic pistols is disclosed, comprising a pair of opposed guide rails **(10)** arranged to support and guide a reciprocating breech **(50)**. The rails **(10)** are joined by a transverse bridge **(20)** positioned to provide structural rigidity and to define a controlled passage for movement of associated operating components. An internal projection **(30)** is formed on or carried by the bridge **(20)** and is configured to cooperate with the breech **(50)** during rearward or forward travel thereof. A feeder **(40)** is disposed beneath or adjacent the breech path and is arranged to present a cartridge toward the breech **(50)**. The internal projection **(30)** selectively engages a corresponding surface of the breech **(50)** to retain, delay, arrest, or release the breech in response to the position of the feeder **(40)** or the operating cycle of the pistol. The arrangement provides a compact breech catching function integrated with the rail and bridge structure, improving alignment, reducing component count, and enhancing reliability during automatic or semi-automatic operation.

**Abstract**

An automatic or semi-automatic pistol is provided with a breech catch mechanism actuated by the last-cartridge feeder for indicating and retaining the open condition of the arm after discharge of the final cartridge. The pistol comprises a frame **(1)**, a barrel and breech assembly **(2)** arranged for rearward and forward movement relative to the frame, a cartridge magazine **(3)** containing a spring-urged feeder or follower **(4)**, and a breech catch member **(5)** mounted in the frame adjacent the path of movement of the breech assembly.

Upon firing of the last cartridge, the magazine feeder **(4)** rises to its uppermost position and engages an actuating projection or lever **(6)** associated with the catch member **(5)**. This engagement displaces the catch member upwardly or pivotally into the path of a cooperating shoulder, recess, or abutment **(7)** formed on the breech assembly **(2)**. During the recoil or rearward movement of the breech assembly, the catch member **(5)** enters into engagement with the abutment **(7)** and prevents the breech from returning to its closed position.

The catch member **(5)** is shaped so that, when engaged by the breech assembly **(2)**, it exerts an upward supporting action on the forward or rearward portion of the breech, thereby causing the breech to assume a visibly tilted upward position relative to the frame **(1)**. The tilted position exposes the chamber region and provides a clear indication that the magazine is empty and that the breech is retained open. A retaining surface **(8)** on the catch member cooperates with the abutment **(7)** to hold the breech assembly securely in the raised position until manually released.

A manual release portion **(9)** may be provided on the catch member **(5)** to permit the operator to depress or disengage the catch after insertion of a loaded magazine or upon inspection of the pistol. The mechanism thus automatically arrests and elevates the breech after the last cartridge has been fed and fired, while permitting subsequent release by manual operation.
